title: Learn GitHub Actions
subtitle: A short, practical guideline. This site is static on purpose, so the interesting part is the CI/CD you build around it.

sections.title: 1. What is GitHub Actions?
body: GitHub Actions is GitHub's built-in automation platform. You describe automation in YAML files called workflows, stored in .github/workflows/ in your repository.
A workflow runs when an event happens (a push, a pull request, a schedule, a manual click) and executes one or more jobs on machines called runners.

sections.title: 2. Core concepts
list: Workflow: a YAML file in .github/workflows/ describing the automation.
Event (on:): what triggers the workflow, e.g. push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, schedule.
Job: a group of steps that runs on one runner. Jobs run in parallel unless you add needs:.
Step: a single shell command (run:) or a reusable action (uses:).
Action: a reusable unit, e.g. actions/checkout or actions/setup-node.
Runner: the machine that runs a job, e.g. ubuntu-latest (GitHub-hosted) or a self-hosted machine.

sections.title: 3. Your first workflow
body: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml with the content below. It installs dependencies, type-checks, tests and builds this site on every push and pull request.
sections.code:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm
      - run: make ci

sections.title: 4. Common triggers
list: push / pull_request: run on code changes; filter with branches: and paths:.
workflow_dispatch: adds a 'Run workflow' button in the Actions tab (with optional inputs).
schedule: run on a cron expression, e.g. '0 3 * * *' (UTC).
release / tags: run when you publish a release or push a tag like v1.0.0.

sections.title: 5. Ideas to practise with this repo
list: Cache dependencies with actions/setup-node's cache: npm and compare run times.
Use a matrix to test on Node 20, 22 and 24.
Upload the ./out folder with actions/upload-artifact.
Deploy ./out to GitHub Pages with actions/upload-pages-artifact and actions/deploy-pages.
Split lint/test/build into separate jobs connected with needs:.
Add concurrency: to cancel outdated runs on the same branch.
Store a value in Settings > Secrets and read it with ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}.
Build a Docker image and push it to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).

sections.title: 6. Tips
list: Pin actions to a major version (@v4) or, for maximum safety, a full commit SHA.
Give workflows least privilege with a top-level permissions: block.
Keep CI logic in the Makefile so it runs the same locally and in CI: make ci.
Read logs in the Actions tab; re-run failed jobs with debug logging enabled.
